sections.title: Andean giant
sections.text: Native to the high, dry Andes of Peru and Bolivia, this monocarpic bromeliad forms a dense rosette and may reach about 15 m including its flowering spike. The spike can carry as many as 20,000 flowers, each about 5 cm across.

sections.title: Life cycle
sections.text: It flowers once, often only after many decades, then the flowering plant dies. Its capsules produce millions of seeds, but natural germination is uncommon. Human food uses or toxicity were not verified.

sections.title: Image details
sections.text: The plate shows the characteristic massive upright spike, narrow spiny leaves, pale flowers, and a capsule with seeds.
